To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of OCs in young women is associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.
the effects of OCs on endogenous hormones and body constitution are not the same in present, former, and never users, which may explain the different health risks of OC use.

(i) OCs may induce a rebound increase in FSH concentrations after cessation of use, (ii) OCs may cause weight gain and increase breast size and (iii) OC use before the first fullterm pregnancy is related to increased proliferation rate in breast epithelium, and (iv) women with a first and/or a second degree relative with breast cancer and who use exogenous hormones may also have a higher proliferation rate
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of OCs and other exogenous hormones on endogenous hormones and breast epithelium in healthy, young women.
the effects of low doses of OCs on endogenous hormones and on body constitution in healthy young women.
the long term consequences of OCs on the endocrine system, and on the body constitution, especially the breast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OCs do not have a significant effect on the proliferation rate in normal breast tissue.
OCs may increase the risk for breast cancer in some women, especially those who use OCs before their first full term pregnancy.
OCs have no effect on breast epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of OCs in young women may increase the risk for breast cancer, and that intermittent use of OCs may be particularly hazardous.
OCs affect endogenous hormones in a way that is dependent on OC dose, duration and timing in relation to the menstrual cycle.

OCs may affect the breast tissue, especially in women who use OCs before the onset of the first full term pregnancies, who have a family history of breast cancer, and/or who have a high body constitution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
OCs have an effect on breast epithelial proliferation.
OCs have effects on endogenous hormones that are not related to the estrogenic potency of the compounds.
OCs affect the hormonal environment of the breast.
